content: Safe areas and mobile viewport heights: viewport-fit=cover on the viewport meta opts the page into edge-to-edge layout, after which env(safe-area-inset-top/right/bottom/left) must be respected manually; browsers that do not know env() drop the whole declaration containing it, so always write a plain fallback declaration first, and combine insets with minimums via max(0.75rem, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)). 100vh equals the LARGE viewport (lvh) and is covered by expanded mobile browser toolbars; 100svh is the stable small viewport (never obscured, may leave blank space), 100dvh tracks the dynamic viewport but resizes while scrolling (jank/perf cost). svh/lvh/dvh are supported Safari 15.4+, Chrome 108+, Firefox 101+ (Baseline widely available). For an app-shell that scrolls internally (h-screen overflow-hidden), swapping to h-dvh is a no-op on desktop (no dynamic chrome) and fixes the mobile toolbar cover problem.
